minutes.headline: Select Board split 2-2 on sending TC Passios renovation and new-build articles to special town meeting; decision put off to Oct 5.
minutes.summary: The board met with the TC Passios building design committee about three possible special town meeting articles: a status update, renovation funding, and new-build design funding. Members were evenly divided on timing, so no vote was taken and the matter was put on the next agenda. The board also heard about an elderly exemption increase, approved a road closure and the advertising of a parcel, and objected strongly to a draft demolition delay bylaw change.

public_comment.topic: A board member reflected on a cemetery dedication and 9/11 (mr jeffries, an official).
Announced an Oct 28 joint Finance and School Committee meeting on Chapter 70; separately urged not rushing the TC Passios articles to special town meeting.

votes.motion: Block off Memorial Drive Oct 23, 6:30 to 9:30 pm, for the Boys and Girls Club Shrieks and Creeks event.
Authorize the town manager to advertise parcel 7 as part of the disposition of 671 West Street.
Enter executive session under MGL c.30A s.21 reason 6 regarding 665 Mass Ave, and adjourn afterwards.

budget_items.what_was_said: The assessors propose raising the exemption and formalizing the income and asset guidelines at town meeting. It is partly reimbursed through the cherry sheet in a variable amount.
Town meeting authorized a study of the cost to build new instead of renovating.
Article 2 would ask for construction funding for the renovation, based on a two-year study.
Article 3 would fund design development for a new build. The committee said it would cost a few hundred thousand more, and that escalation is about four percent a year.
The new growth figure submitted to DOR exceeds the town meeting estimate and eliminates a deficit caused by final state aid figures and school choice and charter assessments.
A cost estimate is expected in time for the fiscal 23 capital planning process.
The state closed FY21 with a surplus, and the MMA asked for added Chapter 90 funding. ARPA funds may bring matching programs.
Draft would add a daily fine for violations. Members called it excessive.

budget_items.what_was_said: A resident put the cost of space for the extended day program above one million dollars.

decisions.decision: Board will not vote on the TCP articles tonight; the item goes on the Oct 5 agenda and the committee is invited to attend.
A member agreed to ask the School Committee for its position on the town hall and other uses at the TCP site.
The demolition delay bylaw article waits for town counsel's review; the historical commission is invited to next week's meeting.
Discussion of demolition requests to be picked up at the Oct 5 meeting.

what_happened.line: The Select Board split evenly on whether to send the TC Passios renovation and new-build articles to a special town meeting, took no vote, and put the item on the Oct 5 agenda.
The board heard from the TC Passios design committee about three possible articles: a status update, renovation construction funding, and design funding for a new build.
Members objected to a draft demolition delay bylaw change that would add a daily fine; the article waits for town counsel's review.
The board voted to close Memorial Drive on Oct 23 for the Shrieks and Creeks event, with one abstention.
The board authorized the town manager to advertise parcel 7 as part of the disposition of 671 West Street.

why_it_matters: The TC Passios articles would ask voters for renovation construction money or new-build design money, so the timing of the special town meeting decides when residents are asked to vote on a large capital cost.

The assessors' proposed change to the elderly exemption would go to town meeting, and it is partly reimbursed through the state's cherry sheet in a variable amount, so the net effect falls on the tax bill.
watch_next: The Oct 5 Select Board meeting, where the TC Passios articles return to the agenda and the design committee is invited.
The Oct 28 joint Finance Committee and School Committee meeting on Chapter 70.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on both votes and on nearly all the figures they share. They differ on who chaired and who the principal assessor was, on the date the demolition-delay item returns, and on several TCP items only our recording has. The date and the chair/assessor roles should be checked first.
